newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Lufthansa group wins Manila airport deal.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa group wins Manila airport deal.

text.p: The Philippines is set to award a multi-billion peso airport terminal project to People's Aircargo & Warehousing Co Inc (Paircargo), a consortium in which Lufthansa AG has a stake, an official said.

Transportation undersecretary Primitivo Cal said the contract to build a new terminal at Manila airport was going to Paircargo as a rival bidder, Asia's Emerging Dragon Corp (AEDC), a company owned by the country's six richest Chinese-Filipino tycoons, had dropped out.
"Asia's Emerging Dragon Corp (AEDC) lost its right to match considering that the prescribed period already lapsed on December 3," Cal told reporters.

AEDC was invited by President Fidel Ramos to build a modern terminal at Manila Airport under a build-operate-transfer scheme. The firm had accepted the offer, but Paircargo came in earlier this year and submitted a better bid.

The transportation department asked AEDC to match Paircargo's bid but the group decided not to saying it could not match something it was not aware of. The government had not given enough details on Paircargo's bid, AEDC said.
Paircargo comprises of the biggest cargo warehousing operator in the international airport, Philippine Airport and Ground Services Inc (PAGS) and Security Bank Corp.
PAGS is a joint venture between Lufthansa AG and Paircargo.

Cal said the contract would be drafted after Paircargo had complied with certain conditions including proof of equity build up, firm commitment from financing institutions and posting of performance bonds.
Paircargo executive vice president Gerry Esguerra later told reporters the consortium could easily comply with the requirements. - Manila newsroom 63 2 8418938 Fax 8176267
